faq.question: Why does the log show `unrecognised` Home Connect API keys or union types?
faq.answer:
The plugin maintains an internal schema of the Home Connect API's programs, options, statuses, and their corresponding values. When your appliance reports a state or configuration option that is not yet documented or mapped within the plugin's schema (frequently occurring with new appliance models or firmware updates), the plugin outputs a structured diagnostic block in the log highlighting these values with an `(unrecognised)` comment.

To resolve this:
1. Ensure you are running the latest version of the plugin, as support for newly discovered API values is regularly added in updates.
2. If the unrecognized values persist on the latest release, copy the complete diagnostic block (delimited by the `====================` lines) from your logs and open an issue on the GitHub repository so they can be added to the schema in a future release.
faq.semantic_abstract: Home Connect appliances frequently introduce undocumented API states and options via firmware updates, resulting in the plugin logging auto-generated diagnostic blocks with `(unrecognised)` annotations. Reporting these schema mismatches allows the maintainer to update the internal TypeScript types and incorporate support for the new appliance features.
